title: Bonding, Shapes of Molecules and Energetics
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Chemistry: Bonding and Energetics Worksheets
standard_text: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, shapes of simple molecules and ions, bond polarity and intermolecular forces, enthalpy change, calorimetry, Hess's law, enthalpies of formation and combustion, and mean bond enthalpies.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level chemistry worksheets on bonding and energetics: shapes of molecules and bond angles, intermolecular forces, calorimetry, Hess's law and mean bond enthalpies. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Electron pairs repel: lone pairs repel most.
body_html:
How to think about it

The shape of a molecule depends on the number of electron pairs round the central atom. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the bond angle by about 2.5° (CH₄ 109.5°, NH₃ 107°, H₂O 104.5°).

In calorimetry q = mcΔT and ΔH = −q/n. By Hess's law, ΔH = ΣΔfH(products) − ΣΔfH(reactants). With bond enthalpies, ΔH = bonds broken − bonds made.

Example

Shape of NH₃?

3 bonding pairs, 1 lone pair

Answer: pyramidal, 107°

Example

0.46 g of ethanol heats 100 g of water by 20 K. ΔH?

q = 100 × 4.18 × 20 = 8360 J

n = 0.0100 mol

Answer: −836 kJ mol⁻¹

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the minus sign for an exothermic ΔH.
  • Using the mass of fuel instead of water in q = mcΔT.
  • Doing reactants − products in Hess's law.

faq.q: Why does a lone pair reduce the bond angle?
faq.a: Lone pairs are closer to the central atom and repel more strongly than bonding pairs.
The enthalpy change of a reaction does not depend on the route taken, as long as the start and end are the same.

items.q: Why can metals be hammered into shape?
c: layers of positive ions can slide over each other
the electrons are fixed in place
items.e: The delocalised electrons hold the ions together as layers slide.

items.q: What is the bond angle in CH<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: 4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: Which change makes a molecule's van der Waals forces stronger?
c: a longer chain with more electrons
items.e: Straight long chains have more surface contact.

items.q: What is the strongest type of intermolecular force?
items.e: Covalent bonds are within molecules, not between them.

items.q: Why does diamond have a very high melting point?
c: many strong covalent bonds must be broken
items.e: Diamond is a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

items.q: What is the shape of NH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs around the central atom: bent (non-linear).

items.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity?
c: its layers are held by covalent bonds
it has delocalised electrons between the layers
items.e: Each carbon uses three electrons in bonds; the fourth is delocalised.

items.q: What is the shape of SF<sub>6</sub>?

items.q: Which substance has hydrogen bonding between its molecules?
items.e: Hydrogen bonding needs H bonded to N, O or F.

items.q: What is the bond angle in XeF<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: 4 bonding pairs, 2 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What is a co-ordinate (dative covalent) bond?
c: a bond with three shared pairs
a shared pair of electrons where both electrons come from one atom
items.e: For example the bond from N to H⁺ in NH₄⁺.

items.q: Which molecule is polar?
items.e: CO₂, CCl₄ and BF₃ are symmetrical, so the dipoles cancel.

items.q: What is the bond angle in H<sub>2</sub>S?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs, 2 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What kind of structure does iodine have?
items.e: Weak van der Waals forces between I₂ molecules, so it sublimes easily.

items.q: Why does magnesium have a higher melting point than sodium?
c: Mg²⁺ has a larger charge and there are more delocalised electrons
items.e: Stronger metallic bonding.

items.q: Which substance conducts electricity when molten but not when solid?
items.e: Ions are fixed in the solid but free to move when molten.

items.q: What is the bond angle in PCl<sub>5</sub>?
items.e: 5 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What is electronegativity?
c: the energy to remove an electron
the power of an atom to attract the pair of electrons in a covalent bond
the number of bonds an atom forms
items.e: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

items.q: What type of bonding is in sodium chloride?
items.e: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

items.q: Why does ice float on water?
c: ice has covalent bonds between molecules
hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in an open lattice
items.e: Ice is less dense than liquid water.

items.q: Use enthalpies of combustion (kJ mol⁻¹): C −393.5, H₂ −285.8, CH<sub>4</sub> −890.30. Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>).
